attribution.note: Marcus wrote this in his own Substack post. The quotation inside it is the paper's wording, but the criticism ('oversold', 'dubiously alleged') is his own.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the paper's hedged wording and Marcus's evaluative framing. It is a retrospective assessment of a 2023 paper. Its core is an evaluative judgment about how well the evidence supported the paper's claim, not a testable fact.

contract.note: The contract is right that 'oversold' and 'dubiously' name no standard of evidence and that 'early, incomplete AGI' has no threshold. Choosing either would decide the verdict. Checking that the quote is accurate does not test the criticism. Treating the claim as not scorable is fair.

evidence.note: This is the paper's own admission that its method is subjective and informal. That is relevant to whether it was oversold, but it does not settle whether its qualified AGI characterisation was justified.

reviews.rationale: Marcus's claim that the Sparks paper was oversold and its AGI claim dubious is an evaluative judgment with no stated standard. The packet shows the paper hedged its claim and admitted its method was informal. That is context, not a verdict on whether the evidence justified the claim. Any decisive standard would have to be imported from outside his words, so the claim cannot be scored.
